value.rationale: The result gives a universal one-frequency sharp admissibility test for every positive summable Poisson mixture, a natural broad class of circular smoothing/covariance kernels. The boundary is structurally singular: a single scale loses an infinite high-frequency tail and finite-set strict definiteness, while any nondegenerate scale mixture has only the two designated Fourier notches and is strictly positive definite; the exact positive two-scale formula quantifies their reopening. A constructive positive log-convex non-moment counterexample shows this is a genuine moment-structure theorem rather than a generic positivity check. The classification can guide spectral covariance design and interpolation conditioning.
